orquestadores.meta: Nobody who matters goes cold: every meeting arrives prepared, every promise gets its follow-up, and your network grows with intent.
What you owe and what you're owed gets done on time — classes, Northbeam outreach, and the things others promised you.
You think better each week: what you read stays, what you study solves a real problem, and the council keeps your direction above your tasks.
The machinery runs on its own: fresh copies of every channel, a second brain that stays text and in sync, backups, and an Architect that fixes what breaks.

canales.que: The meetings copy came back empty on Wednesday morning, so Conversations and the English coach had nothing to read. Channels now retries once and writes a notice instead of an empty file.

coach.que: With an empty meetings copy the coach skipped its lesson instead of failing loudly. It now waits for the Channels retry and only skips if the copy is still empty.

platicas.que: It stopped on an unnamed speaker in Tuesday's call. It now matches the calendar invite first and only asks you when the invite has more than one outside guest.

linkedin-mac.que: LinkedIn showed a sign-in check on Wednesday and the agent stopped, as it should. It now waits a day and tries once with a slower pace; if the check returns, it leaves it for you again.

cabina.que: Saturday has the Founders' Table demo night and a CS 210 proposal revision due Sunday; both claim the afternoon.
cabina.extra: On days like this, should demo night go first on your day's view, or the class deadline?

historia.que: Channels: retries the meetings copy once before writing, and leaves a notice instead of an empty file — Conversations and the English coach no longer start from nothing.
Conversations: names an unclear speaker from the calendar invite before asking you; asks only when two or more outside guests could fit.
LinkedIn (Mac half): after a sign-in check it waits a day and retries once at a slower pace, then stops for you.
Outreach: no generic openers — every first email must name one concrete thing about the firm, or it's held back.
Your hours: compares last week's hours with your declared focus, in one line on Monday.
Weekly close: asks about people who went quiet this week, not only goals and promises.
Introductions: twice a week suggests two people in your CRM who should meet, with a two-line intro you could send.
The agents page reads the list of agents from their own files, so adding or retiring one shows up everywhere at once.
Your day's view: priority-1 tasks now sit above the calendar.
Meeting prep: every brief ends with the one thing to get out of the meeting.
Meeting prep (Mac half): adds the latest WhatsApp thread and files to each brief.
Orchestrators replace the old groups: each one is a goal of yours plus the agents that serve it.
Waiting for: drafts a short nudge for anything owed to you that's gone quiet, with the date to send it.
English coach: one pattern a day, only if it would cost you in a real business meeting.
Trust scores: each agent is scored over 14 days on how often it runs, how often you approve it as is, and how carefully you decide.
Classes: reads your course sites and syllabi and lists what's due this week.
Your council: the Strategist and the Philosopher write you one thing each morning.
Study queue: turns each link into an 80/20 note and offers one deep session a day.
